padmanabha_mandapa.label: Mandapa of the Padmanabhaswamy temple at night
padmanabha_mandapa.anchor: The great pillared mandapa of the Padmanabhaswamy temple: carved granite pillars receding into shadow, a polished granite floor that doubles every flame, brass oil lamps along every wall and pillar, and at the far end the sanctum doorways above a low granite platform. Every man inside is barefoot and bare-chested in a fine mundu and shoulder cloth, and the open outer doorway shows a silver sheet of monsoon rain.
padmanabha_mandapa.absent: No shirts, coats, turbans, crowns or footwear inside the temple, no glass lamps or lanterns, no chairs or throne and no Europeans. The god is never shown whole, only as fragments of gold and shadow through the sanctum doors.
padmanabha_mandapa.time: night, brass open-wick lamps reflected in the stone floor

temple_vault.label: Treasure vault beneath the temple floor
temple_vault.anchor: A low stone vault beneath the flagged temple floor, almost wholly black: heaped gold coins of many old realms and iron-bound wooden chests catch a single thread of light at the centre of the strip.
temple_vault.absent: No figures, skeletons, steel doors, modern safes or lamps inside the vault; every coin face is worn smooth, with no legible letters or numerals.
temple_vault.time: darkness pierced by one thin thread of light

temple_corridor.label: Pillared corridor around the temple
temple_corridor.anchor: The long pillared corridor that runs around the temple, seen from high above: two receding ranks of carved granite pillars, brass lamps burning in two long lines, a polished stone floor, and beyond the outer wall the rain-dark leaves of the serpent grove.
temple_corridor.absent: No crowd in the aisle, since the nobles stand only at its edges; no glass lamps, railings, footwear or second sweeping figure.
temple_corridor.time: night, lamplight inside and rain beyond the outer wall

fort_courtyard.label: Travancore fort courtyard
fort_courtyard.anchor: The flagstoned courtyard of a Travancore fort, laterite walls, a doorway into the fort buildings and a gatehouse under a sloping tiled roof, with the red Travancore banner bearing a silver conch lifting above the gate. Revathi and Nagoji keep a long stretch of flagstone between them in every view and never touch.
fort_courtyard.absent: No lettering on the banner, no second banner, no blue-coated or red-coated soldiers, no glass lanterns and no bystanders crossing between the two of them.
fort_courtyard.time: early evening, low gold light from the gate side

mavelikkara_pavilion.label: Treaty pavilion at Mavelikkara
mavelikkara_pavilion.anchor: An open-sided Travancore pavilion at Mavelikkara on timber posts under a sloping tiled roof, one cloth-covered table at its centre with the treaty sheet, quill and inkpot, and Company soldiers in blue coats standing at the back.
mavelikkara_pavilion.absent: No lettering on the document or on any flag, no British red coats, no ships or harbour, no throne and no royal figure at the table.

night_rampart.label: Travancore fort rampart at night
night_rampart.anchor: The wall walk and parapet of a Travancore fort after rain, the dressed stone still wet, looking out over a dark kingdom: the small lamps of distant forts on the hills, the pale line of a road and the ordered cookfires of an army camp below.
night_rampart.absent: No glass lanterns, no sentries or third figure on the wall, no ships, and no memory figure outside the one stain panel that asks for it.
night_rampart.time: night after rain, faint lamp and cookfire glow

udayagiri_chapel.label: Chapel at Udayagiri Fort
udayagiri_chapel.anchor: A quiet corner of Udayagiri Fort at the foot of its hill: a small chapel of local granite with a simple wooden cross above its door, a plain altar and a front pew inside, and the fort's granite walls rising behind. Whenever all three men share a frame, the order left to right is De Lannoy, Nagoji, Duarte.
udayagiri_chapel.absent: No stained glass, bell tower, statues, gilding or vestments, no blue-coated soldiers or other worshippers, and no gravestone or lettered stone anywhere yet.

star_fort_rampart.label: Coastal star-fort rampart in later years
star_fort_rampart.anchor: The broad rampart of an angled, bastioned Travancore star fort on the coast: a laterite and granite parapet with gun embrasures, a drill yard and a shore battery below, the surf line and open sea on one side, and roads, fields and distant forts inland.
star_fort_rampart.absent: No British red coats, Dutch blue coats or tricorns on the Travancore troops, no galleons, steamships or lighthouse, and no lettering on any flag.
star_fort_rampart.time: dusk, monsoon clouds building over the sea

war_hall_map.label: Remembered war-hall map
war_hall_map.anchor: A painted map of the south of the peninsula spread on the low Travancore war-hall table, seen from above with the sea to the left: red inland to the north, black far to the north, brown to the east, small blue marks at the coastal forts and many small pale patches crowded along the south-west coast.
war_hall_map.absent: No place names, labels, numerals, compass lettering or pseudo-writing anywhere on the map, and no hands, figures or lamps over it.

interrogation_memory.label: Goa interrogation chamber in memory
interrogation_memory.anchor: The vaulted stone interrogation chamber of the Goa prison from the first chapter, framed low so the ceiling stays out of frame: thick stone walls, a brazier glowing on the far side and a table laid out neatly, with Nagoji seated on a stool, his wrists bound to its legs.
interrogation_memory.absent: No nooses: any rope that shows hangs from an iron ring for binding wrists. No guards or gaoler, no grey, topknot or turban on the young Nagoji, and no present-day figure.
interrogation_memory.time: dim brazier and torchlight, faded like old ink

verandah_memory.label: Revathi's western verandah in memory
verandah_memory.anchor: The western verandah of Revathi's Velinadu house on a wet night: timber pillars, dripping tiled eaves, a raised stone floor slick with rain and the warm glow of brass and clay open-wick lamps.
verandah_memory.absent: No glass lanterns, chairs or European furniture and no third adult; the small running girl is a niece, never drawn as Nagoji's child.

rain_split.label: Kochi garden and Velinadu courtyard under one rain
rain_split.anchor: One panel split down the middle under the same falling rain: on the left, the small walled garden of a modest tiled Kerala house in Kochi with banana plants and herb beds; on the right, a Velinadu courtyard with a pillared verandah and wet stone corridors where children run laughing. Keep Kochi on the left and Velinadu on the right.
rain_split.absent: No European buildings, church towers or ships in the Kochi half, no children in the Kochi half and no painted place names.

page-02-panel-03.lettering_space: Keep the left and right ends of the strip in deep black for the two captions, so no coin sits under the lettering.

page-03-panel-02.lettering_space: Leave the dark space above the nobles' heads clear along the length of the hall, so the king's two balloons can run from the far kneeling figure back toward the viewer.

page-06-panel-03.lettering_space: Leave quiet wall beside Nagoji's set face for two balloons entering from off-panel, keeping the face itself clear.

page-07-panel-05.lettering_space: Leave open evening sky above Revathi at the gate for her two trailing balloons, and a low quiet patch of wall beside Nagoji for his caption.

page-09-panel-03.bleed: Young Savitri laughing in a sunlit courtyard bleeds in behind Varma's close night face like a spreading stain at the panel edge, warm and blurred, never a clean framed flashback.

page-12-panel-02.bleed: A faded memory inset whose edges dissolve softly, with nothing of the dusk rampart inside it.

page-13-panel-01.bleed: Faded, desaturated and bleeding in from the panel edge like old ink, clearly set apart from the rainy present.

page-13-panel-02.bleed: A warm lamplit memory with soft, fading edges, set apart from the grey rain of the present.

page-13-panel-03.lettering_space: Leave a quiet band at the top of each half for its place tag and clear space in the right half for one more caption, with the rain kept light there.

page-13-panel-04.time: steady monsoon rain, grey evening light over the kingdom and the sea

character_notes.nagoji: Thick curled moustache; clean-shaven chin and jaw (light stubble at most in the captivity memory), no beard, facial scar, forehead marks or sacred thread, and a tiny flush gold ear stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. Never a turban in this chapter: first grey at the temples in the temple dress and the white-coat uniform, a grey-streaked topknot with the gold-bordered white mundu in the later years, and black hair loose with no grey in the captivity memory.
character_notes.varma: The varma-v1 face and build, aged: grey hair in a low knot at the back of the head, never the side knot above the ear, bare torso with the sacred thread across his chest and a plain white mundu. No jewels or gold necklaces, and no crown, turban, crest or headband in any panel of this chapter.
character_notes.revathi: Deep indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, the tali on its yellow thread, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets and a sandalwood line at the hairline, with grey threading her black hair. In old age on the Velinadu verandah her hair is grey but still braided with jasmine.
character_notes.savitri: Never drawn as Revathi: no indigo sari, no jasmine braid, no tali and no flat-coin necklace. Her lined face from the previous chapter, made young and laughing in the remembered courtyard, and elderly in plain white in the Kochi garden.
character_notes.ramayyan: Thin, sharp fine features and receding hair, plain unbordered white cloth and a palm-leaf bundle; never the temple priest's face.
character_notes.temple_priest: Only the chief priest before the sanctum takes this face; the other chanting priests, the herald, the young attendant and the nobles never use it.
character_notes.eustachius: Tall, pale grey hair and clean-shaven, in a worn white Travancore coat over a plain buff waistcoat; never a red waistcoat, so he never reads as Nagoji in uniform.
character_notes.duarte: Thin and gaunt with a scholar's stoop, grey tired eyes, ink-stained fingers and a callused right hand, in a plain black cassock with a plain standing collar and a small cross on a thin chain. No white Roman collar tab, no stole or chasuble; white-haired in the present scenes.
